title: Cycle Zipper Strategy for Interleaved Initiatives and Staffing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Create an operational heuristic and lightweight playbook called the 'Cycle Zipper' to manage multiple overlapping initiatives across the same cycle window, enabling predictable staffing allocation, targeted scope cuts, and clear handoffs so that high-priority launches keep their SLOs while lower-priority work degrades gracefully.

Background: We regularly run into side-by-side initiatives (e.g., Dedicated autoscaling, runtime batching improvements, Console rollout) that compete for scarce engineering and design bandwidth. Existing guidance focuses on macro tranche rules but lacks a simple, deterministic method teams can apply mid-cycle to decide which work to push, pause, or compress. The Cycle Zipper aims to be that method: a set of ordered heuristics plus an accompanying lightweight spreadsheet model and decision checklist.

Success metrics:
- 95% of priority-P0 work retains original staffing allocation after the first rebalancing decision.
- Median time to reach a rebalancing decision (from signal to decision) < 48 hours.
- Reduction in mid-cycle emergency scope additions by 30% across participating initiatives.

What we'll deliver:
1) A one-page decision flowchart that teams can follow when competing requests emerge.
2) A small Google Sheets model that ingests per-team FTE, committed points, and candidate scope items to produce suggested scope cuts and 'zipper slots' (interleaving windows).
3) Cut criteria and pre-approved scope buckets (Safe hold, Defer, Cut) with examples tuned for Redwood product themes (runtime perf, Dedicated capacity, Private deployment).
4) Communication templates for PMs to inform stakeholders and to log decisions in Linear.
5) A 30-minute training session and recorded walkthrough for PMs and engineering leads.

Approach and heuristics (draft):
- Rule 1 (Priority anchoring): Anchor on OKR-aligned P0 items; identify which P1 items can be compressed or converted into follow-ups.
- Rule 2 (Zipper slots): Break the cycle into 3 equal 'slots' and interleave smaller initiatives into slot boundaries when full-team allocation is required by a P0.
- Rule 3 (Cost-of-delay scoring): For contested items, use a 3-factor score (customer impact x urgenc y x rollback complexity) to rank candidates for retention.
- Rule 4 (Minimal surface leads): If a higher-priority item needs 2 engineers for 4 weeks, require a documented attempt to reduce to 1 engineer + shadowing before pausing other work.
- Rule 5 (Automatic fallback): If a decision isn't made within 48 hours of the signal, apply the conservative default (preserve P0, defer lowest cost-of-delay P1).

Acceptance criteria:
- One-page flowchart and spreadsheet model published in Confluence and linked from PM templates.
- Two pilot teams (Runtime & Console) adopt Cycle Zipper for Cycle 47 and log at least one rebalancing decision using the checklist.
- Feedback collected and incorporated within two weeks post-pilot.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Teams treat zipper as a hard rule and over-defer important long-term work. Mitigation: Explicit rubric on what constitutes 'long-term strategic' and mandatory review with product leadership for multi-cycle deferrals.
- Risk: Spreadsheet model is misused to justify arbitrary cuts. Mitigation: Keep model purposely opinionated and require a short narrative justification for each recommended cut.

Stakeholders: PM (Asha Patel), Eng leads (Liam O'Connor, Priya Singh), Design (Marco Rivera), People Ops (for headcount awareness), Solutions Eng for customer-facing priorities.

Artifacts:
- Draft PRD (Confluence): https://confluence.company.internal/display/PROD/Cycle+Zipper+Strategy
- Spreadsheet model (Drive): https://drive.google.com/example-cycle-zipper-model
comments: 2025-11-07 - Kickoff: Reviewed problem with Runtime and Console PMs. Agreement to pilot Cycle Zipper for Cycle 47. Action: Liam to draft initial flowchart and Asha to build spreadsheet inputs.
2025-11-09 - Engineering review: Priya S. questions the 3-slot assumption; suggested we parameterize slot count by team size instead of fixed 3. Action: update model with team-size parameter.

2025-11-10 - Design feedback: Marco R. recommends adding an explicit UX timeline template for Console rollouts so that we can compute true cross-team dependencies. Action: add a dependency matrix tab to the spreadsheet.

2025-11-11 - PM review: Added example pre-approved scope buckets for 'runtime perf' and 'dedicated capacity' based on historical rebalances. Uploaded to Confluence link. Requesting review from Product Leadership by 2025-11-13.

2025-11-12 - Trade-off discussion: Decided to keep the 48-hour default decision window but allow extension to 72 hours with lead approval when on-call or FTC events are active. Logged decision and rationale in Confluence.
2025-11-13 - Approval: Product leadership (K. Nguyen) gave verbal go-ahead for pilot. Action: schedule 30-minute training for PMs on 2025-11-17.

2025-11-14 - Pilot prep: Spreadsheet model updated with team-size parameter and dependency matrix. Added a short justification field to each recommended cut to prevent misuse. Created Linear template for logging zipper decisions: PM-ZIP-Template.
Next steps: Run two pilot rebalances during Cycle 47, collect timestamps to validate decision latency SLO, and synthesize feedback for iteration in two weeks after pilots complete.
